title: Best Ski and Snowboard Jackets UK
short: Waterproof, insulated and versatile ski and snowboard jackets for men and women, compared by weatherproofing, warmth and fit.
intro: A good ski jacket balances waterproofing, breathability and warmth differently depending on whether you're piste-bashing or hiking into the backcountry. This guide compares jackets tested on the mountain by Advnture, part of the same publisher as T3 and Tom's Guide, covering hardshells, insulated jackets and budget picks for men and women.

products.name: Rush Jacket (Men's)
products.best_for: Freeride and backcountry skiers who want bombproof weather protection
products.key_spec: Gore-Tex Pro Most Rugged, 80/100-denier fabric, no insulation
products.summary: Advnture found this shell outperformed the rest of its test on weather protection, with a burly, highly abrasion-resistant fabric that shrugs off thick forest or rock faces. The athletic cut leaves room for layering without restricting movement, though it has no insulation and makes a telltale crinkling sound.
pros: Fantastic build quality and abrasion resistance
Athletic cut with room to layer
Fully featured with pit zips and dump pockets

products.name: Khroma Kinetic (Men's)
products.best_for: Skiers who run warm or want hardshell protection in a softshell feel
products.summary: Advnture rated the waterproofing and breathability as exceptional, with a soft, stretchy fabric that moves with the body and never left testers sweaty even during strenuous exertion. It's a minimalist jacket that doubles well as a hiking shell, though it offers little warmth on its own.
cons: Not much warmth on its own

products.name: Hohbiel (Men's)
products.best_for: Advanced skiers who stick to piste runs and want built-in warmth
products.summary: A high-performance resort jacket with body-mapped recycled Primaloft insulation giving more warmth in the core and better breathability elsewhere. Advnture found it comfortable with an athletic fit that never felt bulky, though it's expensive and not really designed for backcountry touring.
pros: Stretchy fabric without the usual crinkle

products.name: Haldigrat HS Hooded Jacket (Men's)
products.best_for: Hard-charging backcountry skiers who generate their own heat while hiking
products.key_spec: 20,000/20,000 waterproof/breathable, three-layer stretch shell, no insulation
products.summary: An impressive weatherproof shell with strong stretch and articulation, well suited to backcountry skiers who work hard enough hiking to stay warm without insulation. Advnture liked the deep pit zips for quick venting, though the dump pocket is shallow and there are no external hand pockets.
pros: Deep pit zips for quick venting
Built-in snow skirt and helmet-compatible hood
cons: No insulation, needs a warm mid layer

products.name: Verbier Infinity Jacket (Women's)
products.best_for: Serious or frequent skiers who want top-tier protection and fit
products.key_spec: Life Infinity waterproofing, synthetic insulation, RECCO reflector
products.summary: Advnture's favourite women's snow sports jacket, so water- and snowproof it handles a blizzard without fuss, with a flattering fit that layers well and enough insulation to stay cosy at rest. A RECCO reflector aids mountain rescue searchability, though it carries a matching premium price tag.
pros: Great fit with room to layer
Life Pocket helps preserve phone battery
cons: Light colourways can reduce visibility in whiteout

products.name: Aphelia Lifaloft Ski Jacket (Women's)
products.badge: Best for seasoned skiers and pros
products.best_for: Guides, seasonnaires and frequent skiers who need heavyweight protection
products.key_spec: Helly Tech Professional waterproofing, Primaloft insulation, RECCO detector
products.summary: Built for skiers out in the elements all day, combining strong waterproofing and warmth with genuine breathability and a light enough build to wear comfortably all day. Advnture praised the articulated sleeves and comfortable cut, though sizing runs on the small side.
pros: Fully waterproof and warm yet breathable

products.name: Anvil Jacket (Women's)
products.best_for: Beginner to intermediate skiers who want a comfortable, affordable puffer
products.key_spec: DWR water-repellent coating, recycled synthetic insulation
products.summary: A comfortable, puffy padded jacket that Advnture's testers found stood out for fit and comfort, with plenty of recycled insulation to withstand cold, windy weather. It's water-repellent rather than fully waterproof, and the boxy design offers less arm articulation than pricier, sportier jackets.
pros: Good looks that double as a casual coat
cons: Arms less articulated than sportier jackets

products.name: Mount Bindo II Waterproof Ski Jacket (Women's)
products.best_for: Buyers who want a ski jacket that doubles as an everyday winter coat
products.key_spec: Omni-Tech waterproofing, Omni-Heat Infinity reflective lining
products.summary: A longer-length, smart-looking jacket that Advnture found kept testers cosy thanks to Columbia's reflective heat-trapping lining, with enough coverage to double as a general winter coat off the slopes. It runs slim, so curvier figures may want to size up.
pros: Doubles well as an everyday winter coat
cons: Slim fit won't suit all figures
Can run too warm for spring skiing

guide.a: A hardshell, like the Arc'teryx Rush or Rab Khroma Kinetic here, has no built-in insulation and relies on mid layers underneath, making it versatile across temperatures and better suited to high-effort backcountry skiing. An insulated jacket, like the Schöffel Hohbiel or Helly Hansen Verbier Infinity, is simpler to wear and suits resort skiing where you're not working hard enough to generate your own heat.

guide.q: What waterproofing rating do I actually need?
guide.a: As a rough guide, 10,000-15,000mm handles light to moderate snow, 20,000mm is a strong all-round rating for most conditions, and 25,000-30,000mm, like the Rab and Artilect here, suits serious backcountry or exposed conditions where you'll face sustained wet weather.

A snow skirt is an inner elasticated hem that stops snow getting up inside the jacket during falls or deep powder, useful for off-piste or powder skiing. Minimalist shells built for high-effort touring, like the Rab Khroma Kinetic here, sometimes skip it since testers found it wasn't needed for their lighter, close-fitting style.

guide.q: Can a ski jacket double as an everyday winter coat?
guide.a: Many can, particularly longer-length or less technical designs like the Columbia Mount Bindo II or TOG24 Anvil here. Minimalist, lightweight shells like the Rab Khroma Kinetic also work well as general hiking or rain jackets, helping justify the cost if you'll wear it beyond ski season.
